findings.topic: Owner levels, finite incidence, admissible local paths
findings.analysis: S_c consists of two adjacent level-j blocks. A fine site within O(d s_c) of an endpoint in Lambda_j cannot leave Omega_(j-1): the gap to its complement is at least ell s_c/L. Nor can it reach Omega_(j+2) through the adjacent inner collar. The explicit ell>=32dL supplies slack for these distances and incident fine bonds. Owner levels are j-1,j,j+1, truncated at the endpoint levels. For any fixed output bond, only finitely many adjacent roots/coarse bonds per level can contain it in S_c. The aligned complete-block geometry also gives bounded admissible paths: each annular portion follows its own coarse lattice, with transitions on aligned interface grids. Such paths may use the adjacent full owner block, including a coarser owner block when needed, and cost a constant depending on d,L rather than eta, scale count, or volume.
findings.consequence: C_geom and D_geom are justified under the stated original geometry and collar. An arbitrary fine-lattice path, or an unrelated eroded/replacement domain, would not justify this step and is not authorized by the proof.
